user.title: Set-up 1 of 4: grid import
user.description: Keeps the mean grid import of every quarter hour below a limit (demand charge). **Needed:** where the grid import comes from, a power sensor of your meter or evcc with a grid meter (or both). **Recommended:** the import counter. Everything else can follow later.

data.name: Name
data.evcc_backup: evcc as a reserve for the grid import

data_description.grid_power: Sensor with the power drawn from the grid (W or kW). Negative values (export) count as 0. Optional if you enter evcc.
data_description.grid_energy: Optional but recommended: the meter's import counter. Makes the quarter-hour energy exact after restarts.
data_description.limit_kw: The quarter-hour average that must not be exceeded.
data_description.margin_kw: The guard aims at limit minus margin.
data_description.evcc_site_url: Optional: take the grid import from evcc (for example http://192.168.1.20:7070). Your own sensor above always wins. If evcc runs on the same machine as Home Assistant (add-on), the address is suggested; clear the field if you do not want it.
data_description.evcc_site_password: Only if evcc asks for a password.
data_description.evcc_backup: While your sensor has no usable value (missing or too old) the guard uses evcc instead of giving everything back. It changes back by itself.

grid_check.title: Set-up 2 of 4: is the sign right?
grid_check.description:
Sensor **{entity}**, now: **{now}**.

There is not enough night-time history yet to check. Rule of thumb: import from the grid must be positive, export negative.

If your meter shows import as negative, tick the box: no template sensor needed.

data_description.grid_invert: On = the sensor counts import as negative (e.g. a meter that shows export as positive).

limit.title: Set-up 3 of 4: the limit
limit.description:
Your highest quarter hour of the last days: **{peak} kW**.

The guard keeps every quarter hour below this mean value. You can change it any time (entity Limit).

data_description.limit_kw: The quarter-hour average that must not be exceeded.
data_description.margin_kw: The guard aims at limit minus margin.

devices.title: Set-up 4 of 4: devices
devices.description:
Added so far: {devices}.

The most important device is usually the wallbox. Pumps, batteries, heating and more can be added later on the integration page.

menu_options.add_evcc: Add the evcc loadpoint (settings taken from evcc)
menu_options.add_wallbox: Add a wallbox (directly via Home Assistant)

add_evcc.title: Which evcc loadpoint?
add_evcc.description: evcc reports several loadpoints. Its name, the currents and whether it can switch phases are taken over.

evcc_device.title: evcc loadpoint
evcc_device.description: The guard sets evcc's maximum charging current (a ceiling, evcc keeps regulating below it) and takes it back. Charging is never stopped. No other integration is needed, the address of evcc is enough.

data_description.priority: 1 = restricted first, 10 = only when nothing else helps.
data_description.evcc_url: For example http://192.168.1.20:7070 (reachable from Home Assistant).
data_description.evcc_password: Only if evcc asks for a password (administrator password).
data_description.max_current: The ceiling the guard gives back to evcc afterwards is the one evcc had before.
data_description.evcc_one_phase: Only works if the charger can switch phases. Off = only throttled.
data_description.power_entity: Optional sensor, for example from the evcc integration of the community. Without it the guard reads the power from evcc.
data_description.allow_entity: Optional. Only while this entity is on.
data_description.observe_only: The guard only writes to the log what it would do with this device. Nothing is sent to it and it does not count as a lever. Good for trying a new device first.
data_description.power_invert: On = the power sensor counts consumption as negative.

add_wallbox.title: Wallbox
add_wallbox.description: The charging current is reduced step by step, if allowed down to 1 phase. Charging is never stopped.

data_description.priority: 1 = restricted first, 10 = only when nothing else helps.
data_description.phase_entity: Optional. Without it the wallbox is only throttled, never switched to 1 phase.

data_description.phases_entity: Optional sensor with the number of phases currently used.

data_description.observe_only: The guard only writes to the log what it would do with this device. Nothing is sent to it and it does not count as a lever. Good for trying a new device first.

grid_check_invert.title: Set-up 2 of 4: is the sign right?
grid_check_invert.description:
Sensor **{entity}**, now: **{now}**.

At night (0 to 5 o'clock, no sun) the sensor shows **{night} kW** on average, i.e. negative. Your meter seems to count import as negative, so “turn the sign round” is ticked.

data_description.grid_invert: On = the sensor counts import as negative (e.g. a meter that shows export as positive).

grid_check_ok.title: Set-up 2 of 4: is the sign right?
grid_check_ok.description:
Sensor **{entity}**, now: **{now}**.

At night (0 to 5 o'clock, no sun) the sensor shows **{night} kW** import on average. The sign is right.

data_description.grid_invert: On = the sensor counts import as negative (e.g. a meter that shows export as positive).

limit_nodata.title: Set-up 3 of 4: the limit
limit_nodata.description:
There is no history for a suggestion yet.

The guard keeps every quarter hour below this mean value. You can change it any time (entity Limit).

data_description.limit_kw: The quarter-hour average that must not be exceeded.
data_description.margin_kw: The guard aims at limit minus margin.

finish.title: May I ask a favour?
finish.description:
An anonymous usage statistic helps me keep developing and running the Viertelstunden-Wächter. Only versions, country and which devices are used are sent, **never** names, measurements or passwords.

Voluntary, and you can switch it off any time. Thank you!

data_description.condition_entity: Optional. The guard only intervenes while this entity is on (e.g. a template that is on when the car may charge from the grid). Off: everything is given back.
data_description.lock_entity: Optional. While this is on, active mode is refused and the guard only observes (e.g. an older guard that is still running).
data_description.notify_services: Optional, comma-separated, e.g. notify.mobile_app_phone. Used when the limit cannot be held.
data_description.startup_mode: Restore = the mode it had before the restart.
data_description.mains_voltage: Voltage of one phase (230 V in Europe). Used to convert amps into kilowatts.
data_description.ai_task_entity: Optional: the AI task entity (Settings > Devices > AI tasks) the explainer uses. You choose the model; the guard has no key of its own.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional: a weather entity. With it the load forecast follows the expected outdoor temperature (heating in winter, air conditioning in summer). Without it nothing changes.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Optional: an outdoor temperature sensor. More exact than the weather entity for learning, and its history lets the correction start at once instead of after some weeks.
data_description.charge_plan_entities: Only for another source: charge plan sensors by hand (attributes windows and departure). Not needed when you chose the car planner.
data_description.planner_entry: Choose the car planner (for example Plugwhen) and the guard finds the charge plans of all its vehicles by itself, also vehicles added later. Until the departure the forecast then knows when each car really charges instead of using the learned wallbox pattern. Without it nothing changes. Suggested automatically if exactly one is installed.
data_description.max_reading_age_s: A grid reading that was not written for longer than this counts as missing: no interventions, everything is given back after 90 seconds. Protects against stale values (a sensor that only updates every few minutes cannot be used for control). 0 = never.
data_description.evcc_site_url: Optional: take the grid import from evcc (for example http://192.168.1.20:7070). Your own sensor above always wins. If evcc runs on the same machine as Home Assistant (add-on), the address is suggested; clear the field if you do not want it.

user.title: Battery
user.description: In an emergency the battery is released so that it feeds the house and lowers the grid import. Enter the settings that release it and the value that does so; the guard remembers the previous values and puts them back.

data_description.priority: 1 = restricted first, 10 = only when nothing else helps (default 10: battery last).
data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the state of charge in %.
data_description.min_soc: The battery is only released at or above this value and given back if it falls below.
data_description.release_entity_1: A number (e.g. maximum output power), a selection (e.g. mode) or a switch.
data_description.release_value_1: The number, the option text (e.g. on) or on/off that releases the battery.
data_description.release_entity_2: Optional, e.g. the mode when the first setting is the output power.
data_description.power_w: How many watts the release lowers the grid import (used for planning and the savings estimate).
data_description.max_off_min: 0 = no limit. After this time the battery is taken back in any case.
data_description.restore_original: On: the values from before the release are put back - but only those still holding the release value. Off: use the script instead.
data_description.off_script: Optional script that runs after taking back, e.g. to let your own automation set the battery.
data_description.allow_entity: Optional. Only while this entity is on.
data_description.reserve_entity: Optional, battery reserve: e.g. maximum output power (a low value) or a mode (standby) that stops discharging for self-consumption.
data_description.reserve_value: The number, option or on/off that keeps the battery charged. The previous value is put back afterwards.
data_description.reserve_lead_min: How many minutes before a forecast risk window the battery is held. Needs the switch Battery reserve before a peak.
data_description.observe_only: The guard only writes to the log what it would do with this device. Nothing is sent to it and it does not count as a lever. Good for trying a new device first.

user.title: Vehicle and charge plan
user.description: Plans when the car should charge so that it reaches its target by the next departure: first from the sun (if a solar forecast is set up in the Energy dashboard), then in the quietest quarter hours that the peak limit allows. The plan is advice; carrying it out is a separate switch (off by default) and needs the start and stop commands below.

data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the car's state of charge in %.
data_description.target_soc: Where the car should be at departure (used if no sensor below).
data_description.target_soc_entity: Optional: a sensor or number that holds the target (e.g. the car's charge limit); overrides the fixed value.
data_description.departure_entity: A time entity (next occurrence is used) or a date-time entity / input_datetime / timestamp sensor.
data_description.connected_entity: Optional on/off entity: on = plugged in. The plan is only carried out while it is on.
data_description.charge_kw_max: What the wallbox delivers at most (e.g. 11 kW).
data_description.charge_kw_min: The lowest power the wallbox can charge with (1 phase, 6 A = 1.4 kW).
data_description.house_base_kw: Consumption of the house during the day that the solar surplus must cover before the car gets any.
data_description.start_entity: A button (pressed), switch, selection or number that lets the car charge.
data_description.start_value: The option text, on/off or number for "allow" (not needed for a button).
data_description.stop_entity: A button (pressed), switch, selection or number that pauses the charging. Without it the plan stays advice.
data_description.stop_value: The option text, on/off or number for "pause" (not needed for a button).
data_description.charge_efficiency: Share of the wallbox energy that reaches the battery (about 90 %).

The plan is advice; carrying it out is a separate switch (off by default) and needs the start and stop commands below.

data_description.soc_entity: Sensor with the car's state of charge in %.
data_description.target_soc: Where the car should be at departure (used if no sensor below).
data_description.target_soc_entity: Optional: a sensor or number that holds the target (e.g. the car's charge limit); overrides the fixed value.
data_description.departure_entity: A time entity (next occurrence is used) or a date-time entity / input_datetime / timestamp sensor.
data_description.connected_entity: Optional on/off entity: on = plugged in. The plan is only carried out while it is on.
data_description.charge_kw_max: What the wallbox delivers at most (e.g. 11 kW).
data_description.charge_kw_min: The lowest power the wallbox can charge with (1 phase, 6 A = 1.4 kW).
data_description.house_base_kw: Consumption of the house during the day that the solar surplus must cover before the car gets any.
data_description.start_entity: A button (pressed), switch, selection or number that lets the car charge.
data_description.start_value: The option text, on/off or number for "allow" (not needed for a button).
data_description.stop_entity: A button (pressed), switch, selection or number that pauses the charging. Without it the plan stays advice.
data_description.stop_value: The option text, on/off or number for "pause" (not needed for a button).
data_description.charge_efficiency: Share of the wallbox energy that reaches the battery (about 90 %).

error.value_number: This setting is a number: enter a number.
error.value_onoff: A switch needs the value on or off.
error.unknown_option: The phase selection has no such option.
error.min_above_max: Minimum current is above maximum current.
error.phase_pair: Phase selection and option for 1 phase belong together.

user.title: evcc loadpoint
user.description: The guard sets evcc's maximum charging current (a ceiling, evcc keeps regulating below it) and takes it back. Charging is never stopped. No other integration is needed, the address of evcc is enough.

data_description.priority: 1 = restricted first, 10 = only when nothing else helps.
data_description.evcc_url: For example http://192.168.1.20:7070 (reachable from Home Assistant).
data_description.evcc_password: Only if evcc asks for a password (administrator password).
data_description.max_current: The ceiling the guard gives back to evcc afterwards is the one evcc had before.
data_description.evcc_one_phase: Only works if the charger can switch phases. Off = only throttled.
data_description.power_entity: Optional sensor, for example from the evcc integration of the community. Without it the guard reads the power from evcc.
data_description.allow_entity: Optional. Only while this entity is on.
data_description.observe_only: The guard only writes to the log what it would do with this device. Nothing is sent to it and it does not count as a lever. Good for trying a new device first.
data_description.power_invert: On = the power sensor counts consumption as negative.

loadpoint.title: Which evcc loadpoint?
loadpoint.description: evcc reports several loadpoints. Its name, the currents and whether it can switch phases are taken over.

error.evcc_unreachable: evcc cannot be reached at this address.
error.evcc_loadpoint: evcc has no loadpoint with this number.
error.evcc_auth: evcc asks for a password, or the password is wrong.
error.min_above_max: Minimum current is above maximum current.
error.not_power: This sensor has no power unit (W, kW or MW). Add unit_of_measurement: W to the template sensor or choose another sensor.
error.looks_inverted: Nearly all values of this sensor are negative. A consumer never feeds in: tick “turn the sign round”.
error.evcc_not_charger: This loadpoint is a heating device (heat pump, heating rod) in evcc, not a wallbox. The guard cannot limit it by a charging current.

create_dashboard.name: Create dashboard
create_dashboard.description: Builds a ready-made dashboard (overview, statistics and forecast) with this installation's entities. The YAML is returned and shown as a notification; paste it into a new dashboard (three dots > Edit > Raw configuration editor). The service never writes into an existing dashboard. Administrators only.

import_history.name: Import history
import_history.description: Seeds the day and month peaks from an earlier measurement (a spreadsheet, an older script). Only raises values; values from hourly data are lower bounds.

days.name: Days
days.description: List of entries with date, kw and at.

months.name: Months
months.description: List of entries with month and peak_kw.

send_week_report.name: Send the weekly report
send_week_report.description: Sends the report of the last full week (or the running week) as a message.

current_week.name: Running week
current_week.description: Only the running week so far instead of the last full week.

push.name: Send the message
push.description: Also send it as a message to the notify services.

export_csv.name: Export as CSV
export_csv.description: Writes the quarter-hour load profile or the daily peaks to config/viertelstunden_waechter/export/ (not a public folder).

kind.name: What
kind.description: quarters = every quarter hour (kept 120 days), days = daily peaks (400 days).

format.name: Format
format.description: standard = comma and decimal point, excel_de = semicolon and decimal comma.

explain_today.name: Explain today
explain_today.description: Asks the AI task for a short explanation of today's interventions (without interventions no AI is asked).

push.name: Send the message
push.description: Also send it to the notify services.

correct_quarter.name: Correct a quarter hour
correct_quarter.description: Replaces a quarter-hour value that was recorded wrong with the value from the meter and works out the day's and the month's peak again. Only for administrators.

start.name: Start
start.description: Local start of the quarter hour, e.g. 2026-11-10T19:15.

kw.name: Value
kw.description: Mean grid import of that quarter hour from the meter, in kW.

send_feedback.name: Send feedback
send_feedback.description: Sends your feedback to the author of the Viertelstunden-Wächter (aiwhatelse.eu). With 'include setup' an overview goes along: which kinds of devices and from which integrations, no names, entity ids or values.

text.name: Text
text.description: What works, what does not, what you would like.

contact.name: Contact (optional)
contact.description: An e-mail address if you want an answer.

include_setup.name: Include setup
include_setup.description: Kinds of devices and their integrations, no names or values.

confirm.title: May I ask a favour?
confirm.description:
An anonymous usage statistic helps me keep developing and running the Viertelstunden-Wächter. Only versions, country and which devices are used are sent, **never** names, measurements or passwords.

Voluntary, and you can switch it off any time. Thank you!
